name: Václav Havel
role: Czechoslovak dissident playwright, last president of Czechoslovakia and first president of the Czech Republic (1989-2003)
summary: Havel was a dissident who made moral responsibility, "living in truth" and civic self-organisation the base of politics, and who distrusted ideology, professional parties and the automatism of technological and consumer society, in the East and the West alike. As president he backed a pluralist democracy with a market economy and a state that looks after the vulnerable, European integration, NATO and humanitarian intervention (Kosovo, and support for confronting Iraq in 2003). He held that human rights rank above state sovereignty, rejected violent change and the death penalty, and condemned racism and the postwar expulsion of the Sudeten Germans.

notes: Havel's mature position is taken from his time in office (1989-2003) and from The Power of the Powerless (1978), which stays his most developed political text. In January 1990 he spoke of dissolving both military blocs; as president he then backed Czech NATO membership (1999) and NATO's Kosovo campaign, which is the position recorded here. Themes searched with little or nothing found on Havel's own position: healthcare, taxation, unions, property, drugs, abortion, same-sex marriage, guns, policing and prisons, immigration, the electoral system and the powers of the presidency, central banking, trade and tariffs. Many answers are therefore null.
